A.explanation: Both $F$ forces are tangential at distance $r$ from X and both tend to turn the disc the same clockwise way, so total is $Fr + Fr = 2Fr$.

B.explanation: Only one tangential force $F$ acts at distance $r$, so the moment about X is $Fr$, not $2Fr$.

C.explanation: The two downward $F$ forces give opposite senses about X, $+Fr$ and $-Fr$, so they cancel to zero resultant moment.

D.explanation: Three tangential $F$ forces all act in the same rotational sense, giving about $3Fr$ about X, not $2Fr$.

hints: Look at where each force $F$ touches the disc edge and whether its line is tangential with perpendicular distance $r$ from X.
Recall moment about X is $F$ times perpendicular distance from X, with maximum $Fr$ for a tangential force and zero if the line passes through X.
Give clockwise moments one sign and anticlockwise the opposite sign, then add the two $Fr$ contributions in each diagram to find magnitude $2Fr$.
walkthrough: The disc has radius $r$ and centre X, so any force applied tangentially at the edge has perpendicular distance $r$ from X.
Use moment $=$ force $\times$ perpendicular distance from the pivot, $M = Fd$, with clockwise taken as one sense and anticlockwise as the opposite sense.
In arrangement A the left $F$ acts up and the right $F$ acts down, both tangential, so each gives magnitude $F \times r = Fr$.
Check senses: left-side up and right-side down both rotate the disc clockwise about X, so they add: $Fr + Fr = 2Fr$.
By contrast, B gives only $Fr$, C gives $Fr - Fr = 0$, and D has three same-sense contributions of about $3Fr$. This is option A.
